title: Why Some Teachers Continue To Struggle With Classroom Management agement/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Drawing on conversations with many struggling teachers, Linsin identifies five recurring reasons teachers fail to improve at classroom management year after year: being confused (mixing incompatible approaches instead of committing to one), being lazy (wanting a quick fix instead of studying an approach thoroughly), being mistaken (believing their situation is uniquely bad and therefore unsolvable), being full of excuses (mistaking excuses for real reasons a strategy won't work), and being chaotic (unconsciously thriving on drama and self-sabotaging a peaceful classroom). His unifying diagnosis is that all five patterns share a common root: fear of being responsible, since blaming outside forces lets a teacher off the hook. He argues the situations teachers describe as unique have almost always been seen before, and closes with a call to stop lying to oneself and accept the burden of responsibility as the only path forward, regardless of school or circumstance.
points: Picking and choosing strategies from different classroom management philosophies (mixing SCM with PBIS, for instance) confuses students and guarantees failure.
Believing your teaching situation is uniquely difficult and therefore unsolvable is almost always mistaken — the same conditions have been seen by thousands of other teachers.
What teachers often call 'reasons' a strategy won't work for their class are usually excuses, not real obstacles.
Some teachers unconsciously thrive on drama and sabotage their own path to a peaceful classroom because they don't actually want the drama to end.
All five patterns of struggle share one root cause: fear of taking full responsibility, since blaming circumstances lets a teacher avoid accountability.
quotes: So what follows are five reasons why some teachers continue to struggle year after year with classroom management.
You see, they’re not meant to be used together. Each SCM strategy, for example, is made to mesh with and make every other SCM strategy stronger and more effective.
To be successful, you have to be well-versed. You have to know why the strategies work and how best to use them, which takes study and reflection.
Rest assured, the conditions you’re experiencing, no matter how bad they seem, are the same as thousands of other teachers right now.
Deep down they don’t want a peaceful classroom because then there won’t be anything to rail against. So they sabotage themselves.
You have to throw away the deceptions and doubts, embrace the burden and responsibility, and decide: “I can do this and nothing will stop me.
